title: From Disposal Problem to Resource Stream: The Failure of Linear Waste Models
text:
Early urban planning models treated material byproducts solely as waste streams, necessitating linear 'end-of-pipe' disposal solutions. This foundational approach posited that the economic and technological challenges inherent in separating mixed materials meant that discards could only be managed through landfilling or uncontrolled incineration.

This rejection of intrinsic resource value paved the way for modern Circular Economy Modeling. The shift required abandoning the functional premise that waste represents an unrecoverable cost. Instead, it reframes these defunct streams as rich inputs—'Urban Mining' targets—requiring systematic valorization pathways through complex material flow analysis and advanced technological loops.
